title: Quantum-advantage resource of a two-mode Gaussian state: Analytical theory of convex optimization and a Galois no-go for the closed-form solution
abstract: We study the problem of extracting a quantum complexity resource from a mixed Gaussian state of the multimode light. We present the first complete, certificate-checked solution to this problem in a genuinely coupled sector. We carry this out for the two-mode case, the smallest case in which modes are genuinely coupled. Even in this case the solution is highly nontrivial, and we rigorously prove that it cannot be given in a closed form.
summary: This theoretical paper develops a rigorous framework to calculate the 'quantum complexity resource' from mixed Gaussian states of light. By formulating this as a convex optimization problem, the authors derive that while simple cases yield closed-form solutions, the general two-mode case requires finding the root of a high-degree polynomial, proving that no simple analytical solution exists.
main_problem: The paper tackles the problem of quantifying a 'quantum complexity resource' inherent in mixed Gaussian states of multimode light.
main_result: For the two-mode case, the optimal quantum resource cannot be expressed in a closed form using elementary functions; instead, it is determined as the least real root of a degree-12 polynomial.
method: The problem is formulated and solved via convex optimization (SDP), utilizing dual maximization techniques and analyzing necessary conditions derived from KKT multipliers.
model_or_system: The system models multimode light using continuous variables, characterized by the quadrature covariance matrix V. The analysis focuses specifically on the two-mode case where modes are genuinely coupled.
key_observables: Quantum Advantage Resource ($N_q(V)$), $	ext{Tr}(V_{\star q})$, and the degree-12 polynomial $P(x; V)$.
important_parameters: The number of nonclassical directions ($\kappa$), which dictates whether a closed-form solution exists.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on Slater's condition (V must be strictly mixed) and proceeds by analyzing structured regimes ($\kappa=0, 1, 2$) before tackling the generic coupled case.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the optimization problem for the quantum resource to solving it in specific low-dimensional sectors (e.g., $\kappa=1$), culminating in the derivation of a general polynomial equation whose root yields the solution for generic coupled states.
why_interesting: It provides deep mathematical insight into the limitations of finding closed-form solutions for fundamental physical quantities, connecting quantum resource theory to advanced algebraic geometry (Galois theory).
analysis_basis: full PDF text, analyzed in chunks
